newsitem.title: UK: Bass shares slip to four-month low.
newsitem.headline: Bass shares slip to four-month low.

text.p: Shares in brewer to Holiday Inn group Bass Plc slipped 6p to a four month low of 782p in early trade on Tuesday amid worries about beer sales and the company's plans to acquire Carlsberg-Tetley.
"People are a little bit worried that beer volumes might be slightly down and the Carlsberg-Tetley situation does not help," said Dermott Carr, an analyst at Nikko.

On Monday broker Lehman Brothers reiterated its cautious view on the stock, saying the delay in the company getting approval to buy Carlsberg-Tetley (C-T) will dilute earnings per share in fiscal 1997.
"Until the Carlsberg-Tetley deal is resolved, we advise caution," said Frazer Ramzan, an analyst at Lehman.
Bass launched a complex deal to acquire C-T last August and the Monopolies and Mergers Commission handed over its findings on the proposed acquisition to trade secretary Ian Lang a month ago.
An incoming Labour government is expected to view the deal less favourably than the ruling Conservative Party.
